whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Process Automation AP exam for?

personas.label: Salesforce admins deepening automation skills
personas.description: You build flows every week and want to prove you know how to design them well, not just make them work.

personas.label: Consultants implementing automation
personas.description: You move clients off old workflow rules and Process Builder, and design new automation in Flow.

personas.label: Developers choosing between Flow and Apex
personas.description: You want a clear sense of when Flow is enough and when code is the better choice.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Process Automation AP Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: It is a moderate exam for anyone who builds flows regularly. The tricky parts are choosing the right flow type and trigger timing, handling errors, and staying within limits when many records change at once.
bullets: About 65% to pass, roughly 39 correct answers. Check the official guide for the current figure.
Flow types and timing. Record-triggered (before or after save), scheduled, screen, autolaunched and platform event flows.
Good design. Fault paths, avoiding queries and updates inside loops, testing and deployment.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build a few record-triggered flows, including one with a scheduled path and one with a fault path, before the exam. Before you book. Aim for 75% or more on practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Process Automation AP Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions describe an automation need, such as updating a field when a record changes or sending a reminder three days later, and ask which flow type or setting fits.
bestWayToPass: Know before-save vs after-save: Before-save is fastest for updating the same record. After-save is needed for related records, emails and actions.
Learn scheduled and async paths: Run steps later or outside the main transaction.
Add fault paths: Catch errors and do something useful, like logging or notifying an admin.
Bulk-safe design: Never put Get Records, Create, Update or Delete elements inside a loop.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you design automation in Salesforce: choosing the right flow type, handling errors, staying within limits, approvals, and knowing when Apex is the better tool.

keyConcepts.h2: Process Automation AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Flow Builder: Types & Trigger Contexts
blocks.body: **Record-triggered flows** run when a record is created, updated or deleted. **Before-save** flows (fast field updates) change fields on the same record before it is saved, and are very fast. **After-save** flows run after the save and can update related records, send emails and call actions. **Scheduled paths** run part of the flow later, such as three days after a case is opened. **Screen flows** guide users through steps. **Schedule-triggered** flows run at set times over a batch of records. **Autolaunched** flows run from other flows, Apex or buttons. **Platform event-triggered** flows react to events.

blocks.heading: Advanced Flow Patterns
blocks.body: Use **subflows** to reuse common logic in several flows. Use **collections** to work with many records at once: gather records in a loop, then do one Update Records at the end. **Decision** elements branch the flow. **Run asynchronously** paths move slow work, like callouts, out of the main transaction. **Flow Orchestration** coordinates multi-step, multi-person processes, such as onboarding, with stages and steps assigned to different users. Entry conditions should be as tight as possible, so flows only run when they need to.

blocks.heading: Approval Processes & Entitlements
blocks.body: **Approval processes** route records, like discounts or expenses, to the right people for sign-off, with actions on approval or rejection. Newer **flow-based approvals** give more flexibility for complex routing. In Service Cloud, **entitlements** and **milestones** track service levels, like first response within four hours, and can trigger actions when time is running out. Choose the tool that matches the need rather than building everything in one flow.

blocks.heading: Triggered Automation: Apex Triggers
blocks.body: Flow covers most automation, but **Apex** is better when logic is very complex, needs heavy processing of large data sets, or must do things Flow can't. If an object has both triggers and flows. Know the **order of execution**: before-save flows run before before triggers, and after-save flows run after after triggers. Too many automations on one object make it hard to know what runs when, so keep automation per object organised, often with one flow per trigger type and clear entry conditions.

blocks.heading: Testing, Debugging & Best Practices
blocks.body: Use **Debug** in Flow Builder to run a flow step by step and see the values. **Flow tests** check that record-triggered flows behave as expected and can be run before deployment. Add **fault paths** to elements that can fail, so the flow logs the error or tells someone instead of showing a generic error. Deploy flows with change sets, the Salesforce CLI or DevOps Center, and activate the right version. Old **workflow rules** and **Process Builder** are retired, and the Migrate to Flow tool helps move them.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Process Automation Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions give a business rule in plain words. Decide when it should run, what it touches, and what happens if it fails.

blocks.heading: Know All Flow Types & Triggers
blocks.body: Record changes: record-triggered. Fixed times: schedule-triggered. Users clicking through steps: screen. Called by something else: autolaunched.

blocks.heading: Before-Save vs. After-Save Trade-offs
blocks.body: Updating fields on the same record: before-save. Anything else, like related records or emails: after-save.

blocks.heading: Error Handling with Fault Paths
blocks.body: Add fault paths to data and action elements. Log the error or notify an admin so problems don't go unseen.

blocks.heading: Collections & Governor Limits
blocks.body: Gather records in a collection inside the loop, then update them all at once after the loop.

blocks.heading: Flow Testing & Deployment
blocks.body: Use Debug and flow tests before deploying. Activate the right version after deployment.

nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Process Automation:

sampleQuestions.question: When an Opportunity is saved, its Region field should be set from the owner's country. Nothing else changes. Which flow is the best fit?
options: A before-save record-triggered flow on the object
An after-save record-triggered flow on that same object
sampleQuestions.explanation: Before-save flows update fields on the same record very quickly, without an extra save.
whyWrong: Screen flows need a user to click through.
After-save works but adds another update and is slower for this job.
Scheduled flows run at set times, not on save.

sampleQuestions.question: When a Case is closed, a follow-up Task must be created on the related Account. Which flow fits?
options: An after-save record-triggered flow on that same object
A before-save record-triggered flow on the object
sampleQuestions.explanation: Creating related records needs after-save, because the triggering record must be saved first.
whyWrong: Before-save flows can only change the record that triggered them.
Scheduled flows don't react to the save.
No platform event is involved here.

sampleQuestions.question: A reminder email should go to the case owner if a case is still open three days after it was created. What should be used?
options: A scheduled path on the flow
A before-save flow placed on that object
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scheduled paths run part of a record-triggered flow at a set time after the trigger, with conditions checked again.
whyWrong: Screen flows need a user.
Manual reminders are easy to forget.
Before-save flows run straight away.

sampleQuestions.question: A flow loops over 300 Contacts and runs Update Records inside the loop. It fails during a data load. What is the fix?
options: Collect the Contacts in the loop, then update once after it
Split the single flow out into some three hundred separate flows
sampleQuestions.explanation: Updating inside a loop uses one DML statement per record and hits limits. One update after the loop is bulk-safe.
whyWrong: 300 flows is impractical and doesn't fix the design.
The loop is needed to process each Contact.
Pause doesn't fix DML in loops.

sampleQuestions.question: A flow's Create Records step sometimes fails, and users just see a generic error. What should be added?
options: A fault path that logs and notifies
A second Create Records element in the flow
sampleQuestions.explanation: Fault paths catch errors so the flow can handle them, such as logging details or sending a notification.
whyWrong: Pause doesn't handle errors.
An empty decision does nothing.
Another create step would fail the same way.

sampleQuestions.question: The same address-validation logic is needed in four different flows. What is the best design?
options: Copy the logic into all four flows
Build it once as a subflow and call it from each flow
Ask each one of the users to check the addresses by hand
Move it into a validation rule
sampleQuestions.explanation: Subflows let you build and maintain shared logic in one place.
whyWrong: Copies must all be changed whenever the logic changes.
Manual checks are unreliable.
Validation rules can't call outside services or run steps.

sampleQuestions.question: A flow must call an outside system after a record is saved, and the user shouldn't wait for it. What should be used?
options: A before-save flow placed on that object
sampleQuestions.explanation: The async path runs after the transaction, so callouts don't slow the save.
whyWrong: Screen flows need a user to run them.
Validation rules can't call outside systems.
Before-save flows can't make callouts.

sampleQuestions.question: Every night at 1 a.m., all Opportunities past their close date should be marked as Closed Lost. Which flow fits?
options: A before-save record-triggered flow on the object
sampleQuestions.explanation: Schedule-triggered flows run at set times over a set of records.
whyWrong: Screen flows need a user.
No event is involved.
Record-triggered flows need a record change to start.

sampleQuestions.question: Discounts over 20% need sign-off from the sales manager and then finance. What tool is designed for this?
options: An approval process or flow approval
A before-save flow placed on that object
sampleQuestions.explanation: Approvals route records to the right people in order, with actions on approve or reject.
whyWrong: Reports show data.
Validation rules can block saves but can't route for sign-off.
Before-save flows can't wait for a person's decision.

sampleQuestions.question: New hire onboarding involves IT, HR and the manager, each completing steps in a set order over several days. What fits best?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Orchestration coordinates multi-step, multi-person processes with stages and assigned steps.
whyWrong: Dashboards show data.
A before-save flow runs instantly and can't wait for people.
Validation rules only check data.

sampleQuestions.question: A support team must respond to Premium customers within four hours, and managers should be warned when time is nearly up. What should be used?
options: A Lead assignment rule on the object
sampleQuestions.explanation: Entitlements and milestones track service levels and can trigger warnings and escalations.
whyWrong: Campaigns are for marketing.
Screen flows need a user.
Lead rules assign leads.

sampleQuestions.question: A business rule needs heavy processing of millions of records with complex logic. What should the architect consider?
options: A before-save flow on each record
sampleQuestions.explanation: Very heavy or complex processing over large data is often better handled in Apex, such as Batch Apex.
whyWrong: Before-save flows run per transaction and aren't built for millions of records at once.
Screen flows are for user interaction.
Fields don't process records.

sampleQuestions.question: An org still has old workflow rules and Process Builder processes. What should be done?
options: Delete all of them without putting anything at all in their place
Leave them as they are forever
Move them to Flow, using the Migrate to Flow tool where it helps
sampleQuestions.explanation: Workflow rules and Process Builder are retired. Flow is the supported tool, and the migration tool helps move them.
whyWrong: Deleting them removes needed automation.
They are no longer being improved and should be moved.
Validation rules can't do what they do.

sampleQuestions.question: Before deploying a record-triggered flow, the team wants to check it behaves correctly for a set of example records. What should they use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Flow tests and Debug let you check the flow's behaviour before deploying.
whyWrong: Layouts arrange pages.
Email templates format emails.
Dashboards show data.

sampleQuestions.question: A record-triggered flow runs on every update to Account, even though it only matters when Industry changes. What should be changed?
options: Add a number of further Decision elements later on in that flow
Turn the flow into a screen flow
Tighten the entry conditions to run only when Industry changes
sampleQuestions.explanation: Entry conditions stop the flow from running at all when it isn't needed, which saves processing.
whyWrong: Decisions later still mean the flow starts every time.
Screen flows need a user.
Pause doesn't fix unnecessary runs.
